headword: {温暖前線|おんだんぜんせん}

definitions.explanation: A boundary at which a mass of warm air moves in and rises over a mass of cooler air. A standard term in weather forecasts and meteorology.

examples.japanese: {温暖前線|おんだんぜんせん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}づいている→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧。
{温暖前線|おんだんぜんせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{通過|つうか}→通過：03506_tsuuka⟧⟦に{伴|ともな}い→に伴い：06804_nitomonai⟧⟦{気温|きおん}→気温：00235_kion⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧。
examples.english: The temperature rises as the warm front passes through.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{温暖前線|おんだんぜんせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{影響|えいきょう}→影響：01877_eikyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{広|ひろ}い→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{範囲|はんい}→範囲：03567_hani⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}る→降る：00839_furu⟧でしょう。
examples.english: Tomorrow, due to the influence of a warm front, rain is expected over a wide area.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{温暖|おんだん}→温暖：02596_ondan⟧ (warm, mild) and ⟦{前線|ぜんせん}→前線：11791_zensen⟧ (front line; in meteorology, the boundary between two air masses). A technical term used primarily in weather forecasts. In Japanese TV weather reports, {温暖前線|おんだんぜんせん} is shown on weather maps as a red line with semicircles pointing in the direction of movement. Warm fronts typically bring gentle, extended rainfall, in contrast to the heavier, shorter downpours associated with cold fronts.
